 MISSOULA, Mont. — Montanans shopping for health insurance are being urged to review plan details carefully during the Affordable Care Act Marketplace open enrollment period.
 The enrollment window runs through Jan. 15, 2027. People who enroll in or change plans by Dec. 15 can have coverage begin Jan. 1. Those who enroll between Dec. 16 and Jan. 15 can have coverage begin Feb. 1, after paying their first premium.
 Montana State Auditor James Brown is warning consumers about plans marketed as “self-funded” or “limited partner” coverage. The Office of the Commissioner of Securities and Insurance says some of these plans may not comply with the Affordable Care Act or provide comprehensive medical coverage, even if they are marketed that way.
 “If a deal looks too good to be true, it probably is. If a health insurance policy offers unusually low premiums and low deductibles yet promises full or unlimited coverage, be skeptical,” Auditor Brown said.
 The agency says it has received complaints from Montanans who believed they had purchased health insurance through a limited partner plan, but later had medical claims denied. Some plans may cover preventive services such as checkups and annual screenings while leaving other medical expenses uncovered. Consumers could be responsible for unpaid bills.
 Regulators say possible warning signs include unusually low premiums paired with promises of full or unlimited coverage, salespeople offering limited partner or “ERISA” plans directly to consumers or claims that a salesperson does not need an insurance license. Consumers should also be cautious if they are pressured to pay a large amount quickly.
 Before providing payment or personal information, the state recommends asking an insurance agent for their full name and National Producer Number. Consumers can check an agent’s license through the Montana Insurance License Search at csimt.gov .
